plans.note: Cap is mutual at greater of 12 months' Fees or USD 1,000,000 (sec-21.1) with Excluded Claims defined in sec-21.3; check that data/security, indemnity, IP and wilful misconduct carve-outs are uncapped and that sec-21.2 preserves incident-response and replacement-service costs as direct damages.

Vendor IP indemnity (sec-20.1) and conduct/data indemnity (sec-20.2) are present; confirm Customer's reverse indemnity in sec-20.3 stays narrow with its exclusions intact, and cross-check the sec-20.5 remedy referenced by sec-9.3.
sec-12.3 expressly preserves our freedom to build, buy and compete; the only countervailing restraint is the exclusivity language in sec-2.2, which should be reviewed under EXCLUSIVITY.
sec-2.2 makes Vendor our sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services — directly contrary to sec-2.1 and sec-12.3 and to the playbook; flag for deletion.
sec-7.2 (first of two 7.2s) obliges us to give Vendor terms no less favourable than any other supplier — wrong direction; sec-12.3 already disclaims any MFN commitment, supporting deletion.
sec-12.4 binds only Customer, runs 18 months post-termination, covers any person employed at any time, and bars engagement with no general-advertising carve-out; needs narrowing and mutuality.

Section 9 provides only cause, insolvency and Customer's special triggers (sec-9.3); no convenience right appears anywhere, so propose inserting a Customer-only termination for convenience on notice with pro-rata refund, keyed to sec-9 and sec-10.2.

sec-8.2 auto-renews 12 months on a 180-day notice window — too long; sec-8.3 uplift (lesser of CPI and 3%, 90 days' notice) is acceptable and can be cited as the pricing-predictability half of the position.
New York law and New York County courts with CISG excluded — within the accepted list and court-based, so likely no change; confirm the sec-28.3 escalation does not delay urgent relief.

sec-24.1 gives us affiliate/successor assignment, sec-24.2 restrains Vendor, and sec-24.4 blocks Vendor exit or repricing on our change of control; verify sec-24.3's catch-all does not swallow sec-24.1 and that sec-13.3 licence transfer aligns.

Ownership of Customer Data (sec-14.1) and Deliverables (sec-14.2) sits with us; watch the Deliverable/Vendor Technology definitions (sec-1.4, sec-1.8), the telemetry carve-out in sec-1.3, and the 'improve the Services' processing right in sec-14.1 read against sec-15.1.

sec-13.1 covers Affiliates and contractors, sec-13.2 gives a perpetual paid-up licence, and sec-13.3 limits suspension to material uncured breach after cure — confirm no at-will revocation remains and that sec-13.4 restrictions are not overbroad.

sec-22.1 allows unlimited, unannounced audits with remote system access — contrary to the playbook and inconsistent with sec-22.2's own limits; propose annual, notified, records-based audits at Vendor's cost per sec-22.2.

sec-7.6 imposes USD 25,000/day liquidated damages on us for dependency delay; delete or convert to relief-from-obligation plus documented time-and-materials cost, and check interaction with the sec-21 caps.

sec-19.1–19.3 give services, conformity, malicious-code and compliance warranties with a 90-day Deliverable period and term-long hosted conformity; sec-19.4 provides repair/re-perform plus refund and is expressly non-exclusive — verify the 90 days is adequate and that sec-19.5's disclaimer does not undercut it.
Coverage lines are present including USD 5,000,000 cyber and USD 2,000,000 E&O, with certificates and a no-limitation-of-liability statement in sec-18.2; check limits against data sensitivity only.

sec-2.1 confirms no minimum quantity or purchase commitment and sec-12.3 disclaims minimum-volume undertakings; only risk is any take-or-pay slipping in via an Order Form, and sec-7.1 bars unlisted minimum-use charges.

Six-month transition assistance (sec-11.1), 30-day data return in machine-readable form with no fee-dispute hostage (sec-11.2) and certified deletion (sec-11.3) are present; confirm sec-10.1's access cut-off dovetails with the transition period.
